calls.head: Stay out of the box, Sharks
calls.body: The Sharks’ penalty kill is near the bottom of the league, and the Oilers’ power play is the best. Discipline matters more than usual for the Sharks tonight. Edmonton has had one of the league’s most effective power plays for years.

calls.beyond: San Jose is one of the league’s heaviest-hitting teams. Even by those standards, this was a lot of hitting: a hit score of 172 in the close stretches of the game, against their usual 116 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 20 games.

surprises.head: San Jose couldn’t get good looks
surprises.body: San Jose’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 3.4% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.2% and a league average of 6.4%. A team strays this far about once every 150 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

story.head: The Oilers take down the Sharks
paras: Mattias Ekholm opened the scoring for the Oilers midway through the first. Vasily Podkolzin made it 2-0 early in the third, and that one stood up as the winner. Alex Formenton scored his first goal for Edmonton two and a half minutes later to make it 3-0. Macklin Celebrini got the Sharks on the board midway through the third.

The Oilers drove the play, and the scoreboard caught up. Tristan Jarry made 19 saves for the Oilers, and Yaroslav Askarov stopped 17 of 20 at the other end. Nobody on the ice had a bigger night than Evan Bouchard, by our Swing measure. The Oil improved to 4-0-1, still first in the NHL in points percentage, while the Sharks dropped to 3-2-0, slipping to fifth in the Pacific.

items.text: Four straight wins for the Oilers.
